## 0de8e68aecee

Two declared axes are inert. `AXES` advertises `gray_skew` and `palette_size`,
but `generate` never reads either value. Same-seed comparisons were byte
identical for `gray_skew="ascending"` versus `"descending"` and for
`palette_size=3` versus `5` in easy, medium, and hard probes. One exact example
is seed 17, sample index 5, medium difficulty; both comparisons return the same
19×25 grid.

This can silently mark misspelled or ineffective curriculum controls as
successful and makes the axis metadata misleading. Reproducible cases are in
`checks/audit/0de8e68aecee_dead_axes.json`.

Suggested repair: either implement observable gray-count ordering and palette
cardinality with `observe_overrides`, or remove the axes. Also reject unknown
keys rather than accepting arbitrary `**overrides`.

## 0de8e68aecee

**Concrete control/domain failure.** The source hash matches the assigned `b852eace1cf5586cd6a5511f1fbe348e8cc02d1cae3f90ea1fa4bff180b4b84b`. With seed 123, sample 7, medium difficulty, `palette_size=3` and `palette_size=5` produce byte-identical grids, and an unknown override key is silently accepted. More seriously, the advertised `grid_h`/`grid_w` valid range is 12..22, but every one of seeds 0--19 at hard difficulty violated that declared domain in at least one dimension; examples include seed 1 at 26x28 and seed 18 at 30x30. Evidence: `checks/audit/0de8e68aecee/case.json`.

This means the public axis contract cannot be used to control or validate the training distribution. A repair should either implement observable palette cardinality and dimensions within the declared range or change the declarations, and it should reject unknown keys.
